Unit 5: Scalable Data Systems

HL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How do we handle Data at Global Scale?

This unit prepares you for the world of Big Data. You will move far beyond simple tables to explore Distributed Systems, NoSQL architectures, and the complex trade-offs between Consistency (ACID) and Availability (CAP Theorem).

You'll start by mastering critical reliability with Transactions (ACID). Then you'll break the single-server limit with Distributed Databases, before exploring modern alternatives like NoSQL and Data Mining.

Transactions (ACID)

Banking relies on this. A group of operations (Transfer: -100 here, +100 there) must succeed or fail as a UNIT.

  • Atomicity: All or nothing.
  • Consistency: The DB remains valid.
  • Isolation: Transactions don't interfere.
  • Durability: Once saved, it's saved forever.
Distributed Databases

When one server isn't enough. We split the data across the world.

  • Replication: Copying data to multiple locations (Safety).
  • Fragmentation: Splitting a table into pieces (Speed).
  • Trade-off: Keeping copies in sync is HARD (CAP Theorem).
NoSQL & Modern Models

SQL is rigid. Sometimes we need flexibility.

  • Document Stores (JSON): Flexible structure (e.g., MongoDB).
  • Key-Value: Ultra-fast lookups (e.g., Redis).
  • Graph: Storing relationships (e.g., Social Networks).
Data Intelligence (Mining)

Turning raw data into knowledge.

  • Data Warehouse: A massive archive of historical data.
  • ETL: Extract, Transform, Load (Cleaning the data).
  • Data Mining: Using algorithms to find hidden patterns (e.g., "People who buy diapers also buy beer").
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Transaction A sequence of database operations treated as a single logical unit.
ACID The set of properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) that guarantee database reliability.
Data Warehouse A large, centralized repository of data integrated from disparate sources, used for analysis.
Data Mining The process of discovering patterns, correlations, and anomalies within large datasets.
Distributed Database A database in which storage devices are not all attached to a common processor (geographic spread).
Replication The process of sharing information to ensure consistency between redundant resources.
NoSQL Non-relational databases designed for unrelated, unstructured, or rapidly changing data.
OLAP Online Analytical Processing. Technology used to organize large business databases and support complex analysis.
